sub_units.name: Transactions: BEGIN, COMMIT, ROLLBACK
sub_units.content: A transaction is a single logical unit of work that contains one or more SQL statements. The BEGIN statement starts a transaction, COMMIT saves all changes made during the transaction permanently to the database, and ROLLBACK undoes all changes if an error occurs, ensuring data consistency.

sub_units.name: ACID Properties
sub_units.content: ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability. These properties guarantee that database transactions are processed reliably. Atomicity ensures all or nothing. Consistency ensures data validity. Isolation ensures concurrent transactions don't interfere. Durability ensures committed changes survive system failures.

sub_units.name: Basic Query Optimization ideas
sub_units.content: Query optimization involves writing SQL that executes efficiently. Best practices include retrieving only necessary columns (avoiding SELECT *), using WHERE clauses instead of filtering at the application level, utilizing appropriate joins, and minimizing the use of subqueries where joins can perform better.

sub_units.name: Index usage in queries
sub_units.content: Indexes are special data structures that improve the speed of data retrieval operations on a table at the cost of slower writes and increased storage space. Understanding when to use indexes, particularly on columns used frequently in WHERE clauses, JOIN conditions, or ORDER BY clauses, is crucial for database performance.

sub_units.name: Real-world SQL problems: Sales analysis
sub_units.content: Sales analysis involves querying databases to find trends, top-selling products, and revenue over time. It typically requires a combination of grouping, filtering, date functions, and aggregate functions to generate actionable business intelligence.
